Maya’s recent work on cloud cost optimization for a high-traffic e-commerce platform stands out. She redesigned infrastructure tagging strategies, cutting monthly spend by 22% without sacrificing performance. Her AWS expertise shone during a critical incident where she rapidly isolated and resolved a billing anomaly, preventing a potential $50K overage.  

Over her four years at CloudOptima, Maya evolved from a focused automation specialist to a strategic contributor. Early in her role, she modernized their CI/CD pipelines using Jenkins and GitHub Actions, reducing deployment friction across 15+ microservices. Her deep Kubernetes knowledge later enabled a seamless migration of a legacy monolith, improving scalability by 40%. She’s also been instrumental in integrating Prometheus and Grafana for real-time monitoring, which became a team standard.  

A standout moment was when she led a cross-team effort to debug a persistent ArgoCD sync failure. Her methodical approach—mapping dependencies, isolating environment variables, and collaborating with upstream providers—resolved the issue in under 12 hours, avoiding a scheduled rollback.  

Maya’s leadership extends beyond technical mastery. She mentors juniors with patience, fostering a culture of ownership. Her ability to balance hands-on troubleshooting with strategic planning makes her a trusted collaborator.  

I wholeheartedly recommend Maya. Her reliability, curiosity, and knack for turning complexity into clarity make her an invaluable asset. She’s the kind of engineer who doesn’t just solve problems—she rethinks the systems around them.
